newsitem.title: CHINA: China says in oil exploitation deal with Iran.
newsitem.headline: China says in oil exploitation deal with Iran.

text.p: China is to help Iran find and exploit oil and natural gas and assist its trade in petroleum products under a deal struck during a visit to Beijing by Tehran's oil minister, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
Xinhua quoted Chinese Premier Li Peng as saying the deal was reached with the state-run China National Petroleum Corp, but gave no further details of the agreement.

"The conclusion of the agreement marks new progress of trade and economic relations between the two countries," Xinhua quoted Li as saying on Monday in a meeting with visiting Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh.
Aghazadeh arrived in Beijing last Thursday to discuss joint oil and gas exploration and boosting his nation's crude oil exports, an Iranian embassy spokesman said earlier.
Xinhua quoted Aghazadeh as saying China had experience in oil prospecting and development, laying the basis for long-term cooperation between the two nations.
China and Iran have no history of joint ventures in the oil sector.
Aghazadeh had invited a delegation of Chinese oil specialists to Iran to hold talks on specific cooperation measures, Xinhua said but gave no details.

The embassy spokesman said last week China was seeking to buy more crude oil from Iran, but declined to say how much additional oil Beijing wanted to buy. Iran currently exports 70,000 barrels per day to China.
China, whose petroleum imports have been rising sharply, would need more oil and gas to help fuel its booming economy, Xinhua said.
"China, while further developing its own petroleum resources, has carried out extensive international cooperation on the basis of equality and mutual benefit," the agency said.
Domestic production, once sufficient to make China a net oil exporter, has been unable to keep pace with surging demand.
Aghazadeh would also meet officials of China's state oil refiner Sinopec before returning to Iran on Tuesday, the embassy spokesman said.
